# Duc - Disk Usage Checker

Duc is a collection of tools for indexing, inspecting and visualizing disk
usage. Duc maintains a database of accumulated sizes of directories of the file
system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create fancy
graphs showing you where your bytes are.

![duc gui](/img/palette-rainbow.png) 

## What is Duc?

Duc is a tool that helps you understand where your disk space is being used. It:

- Indexes your file system to track directory sizes
- Provides multiple interfaces to query and visualize disk usage
- Scales well (tested on systems with 500+ million files and petabytes of storage)
- Creates beautiful sunburst graphs to visualize space usage

## Usage

### Creating an Index

Before you can view disk usage information, you need to create an index:

```bash
duc index /usr
```

This will scan the specified directory and store size information in a database
(default location: `$HOME/.duc.db`).

### Querying the Index

Duc provides several commands to explore your disk usage:

- **`duc info`** - Show available directory trees in the database
- **`duc ls`** - List files and directories with their sizes
- **`duc ui`** - Interactive ncurses-based console interface
- **`duc gui`** - Graphical (X11) sunburst graph interface
- **`duc graph`** - Generate static graph images
- **`duc cgi`** - Web interface via CGI
- **`duc histogram`** - Show file size distribution
- **`duc topn`** - Show largest files
- **`duc xml`** - Export data as XML
- **`duc json`** - Export data as JSON

### Examples

Index your home directory:
```bash
duc index ~
```

List the top-level directories:
```bash
duc ls /
```

Launch the interactive UI:
```bash
duc ui /
```

Create a graph image:
```bash
duc graph /usr > /tmp/duc-graph.png
```

### Configuration

Duc can be configured via configuration files at:
- `/etc/ducrc`
- `~/.config/duc/ducrc`
- `~/.ducrc`
- `./.ducrc`

You can also set the database location using the `DUC_DATABASE` environment variable.

### Common Options

Most duc commands support these options:

- `-d`, `--database=FILE` - Specify database file location
- `-b`, `--bytes` - Show exact byte counts
- `-h`, `--help` - Show help information
- `-v`, `--verbose` - Increase output verbosity
- `-q`, `--quiet` - Quiet mode

### Indexing Options

When creating an index with `duc index`:

- `-e`, `--exclude=PATTERN` - Exclude files matching pattern
- `-x`, `--one-file-system` - Don't cross filesystem boundaries
- `-p`, `--progress` - Show progress during indexing
- `-H`, `--check-hard-links` - Count hard links only once
- `-m`, `--max-depth=N` - Limit directory depth stored in database
- `-u`, `--username=USER` - Index only files owned by specific user

### Visualization Options

For graphical commands (`duc gui`, `duc graph`):

- `--palette=SCHEME` - Color scheme (rainbow, greyscale, monochrome, size)
- `--fuzz=FACTOR` - Adjust visual size calculation
- `--levels=N` - Number of directory levels to show
- `--size=WxH` - Output image size

## More Information

For complete documentation including all commands and options, please refer to
the user manual (`duc.1` man page) in the `doc/` directory.

Check the Duc homepage at http://duc.zevv.nl for additional information.

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the sect

.SH "A NOTE ON FILE SIZE AND DISK USAGE"
The concepts of \'file size\' and \'disk usage\' can be a bit confusing\. Files on disk have an apparent size, which indicates how much bytes are in the file from the users point of view; this is the size reported by tools like \fBls \-l\fR\. The apparent size can be any number, from 0 bytes up to several TB\. The actual number of bytes which are used on the filesystem to store the file can differ from this apparent size for a number of reasons: disks store data in blocks, which cause files to always take up a multiple of the block size, files can have holes (\'sparse\' files), and other technical reasons\. This number is always a multiple of 512, which means that the actual size used for a file is almost always a bit more than its apparent size\.
.P
Duc has two modes for counting file sizes:
.IP "\[ci]" 4
\fBapparent size\fR: this is the size as reported by \fBls\fR\. This number indicates the file length, which is usually smaller than the actual disk usage\.
.IP "\[ci]" 4
\fBactual size\fR: this is the size as reported by \fBdu\fR and \fBdf\fR\. The actual file size tells you how much disk is actually used by a file, and is always a multiple of 512 bytes\.
.IP "" 0
.P
The default mode used by duc is to use the \'actual size\'\. Most duc commands to report disk usage (\fBduc ls\fR, \fBduc graph\fR, \fBduc ui\fR, etc) have an option to change between these two modes (usually the \fB\-a\fR), or use the \'a\' key to toggle\.
.SH "BUILDING from git"
If you use git clone to pull down the latest release, you will have to do the following:
.P
git clone https://github\.com/zevv/duc
.br
cd duc
.br
autoreconf \-i
.P
Then you can run the regular
.P
\&\./configure [ options ]
.br
make
.P

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

* What does the error 'Database version mismatch mean?'
 
  The layout of the index database sometimes changes when new features are
  implemented. When you get this error you have probably upgraded to a newer
  version. Just remove the old database file and rebuild the index.

* Duc crashes with a segmentation fault, is it that buggy?

  By default Duc uses the Tokyocabinet database backend. Tokyocabinet is pretty
  fast, stores the database in a single file and has nice compression support
  to keep the database small. Unfortunately, it is not always robust and
  sometimes chokes on corrupt database files. Try to remove the database
  and rebuild the index. If the error persists contact the authors.

* Some of the Duc subcommands like `duc gui` are not available on my system?

  Depending on the configuration that was chosen when building Duc, some
  options might or might not be available in the `duc` utility. For example, on
  Debian or Ubuntu Duc comes in two flavours: there is a full featured package
  called `duc`, or a package without dependencies on X-windows called
  `duc-nox`, for which the latter lacks the `duc gui` command.

* `duc index` is hogging my system and using a lot of CPU and I/O!

  Traversing a file system is hard work - which is the exact reason why Duc
  exists in the first place. You can use the default tools to make Duc behave
  nice towards other processes on your machine, use something like:

  `nice 19 ionice -c 3 duc index [options]`

  This makes `duc index` run with the lowest CPU and I/O scheduler priorities,
  which is nicer to all the other processes on your machine.

particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

Duc mainains an index of scanned directories, which defaults to ~/.duc.db. All tools
take the -d/--database option to override the database path.

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the section in square brackets and
continues until the next section begins. Sections contain parameters, one per
line, which consist of a single option name for boolean flags, or an option name
and a value for options which take a value. See the EXAMPLES section for an
example of the configuration file format.


## CREATING THE INDEX

Duc needs an index file of the file system before it is able to show any
information.  To create the index, run the `duc index` command. For example, to
create an index of your home directory run `duc index ~`

    $ duc index /usr
    Skipping lost+found: Permission denied
    Indexed 333823 files and 48200 directories, (35.0GB total) in 1 seconds

The default location of the database is `$HOME/.duc.db`. To use a different
database location, use the DUC_DATABASE environment variable or specify the
database location with the --database argument.

You can run `duc index` at any time later to rebuild the index.

By default Duc indexes all directories it encounters during file system
traversal, including special file systems like /proc and /sys, and
network file systems like NFS or Samba mounts. There are a few options to
select what parts of your filesystem you want to include or exclude from the
scan, check the documentation below for the options --one-file-system, 
--exclude, --fs-exclude and --fs-include for more details.


## QUERYING THE INDEX

Duc has various subcommands for querying or exploring the index: (Note that
depending on your configuration, some of these commands might not be available)

* `duc info` shows a list of available directory trees in the database, and the time
  and date of the last scan.

* `duc ls` lists all files and directories under the given path on the console.

* `duc ui` runs a ncurses based console user interface for exploring the file
  system usage.

* `duc gui` starts a graphical (X11) interface representing the file system in
  a sunburst graph. Click on a directory to redraw the graph from the
  perspective of the selected directory. Click in the center of the graph to go
  up one directory in the tree.

## CGI INTERFACING

The `duc` binary has support for a rudimentary CGI interface, currently only
tested with apache.  The CGI interface generates a simple HTML page with a list
of indexed directories, and shows a clickable graph for navigating the file
system. If the option `--list` is given, a list of top sized files/dirs is also
written.

Configuration is done by creating a simple shell script as .cgi in a directory
which is configured for CGI execution by your web server (usually
`/usr/lib/cgi-bin`). The shell script should simply start duc, and pass the
location of the database to navigate.

An example duc.cgi script would be

    #!/bin/sh
    /usr/local/bin/duc cgi -d /home/jenny/.duc.db

* Make sure the database file is readable by the user (usually www-data)
* Debugging is best done by inspecting the web server's error log
* Make sure the .cgi script has execute permissions (`chmod +x duc.cgi`)

Some notes:

* The HTML page is generated with a simple embedded CSS style sheet. If the
  style is not to your liking you can provide an external CSS url with the
  --css-url option which will then be used instead of the embedded style
  definition.

* Add the option --list to generate a table of top sized files and directories
  in the HTML page.

* The options --header and --footer allow you to insert your own HTML code
  before and after the main.

The current CGI configuration is not very flexible, nor secure. It is not
advised to run the CGI from public reachable web servers, use at your own risk.


## A NOTE ON FILE SIZE AND DISK USAGE

The concepts of 'file size' and 'disk usage' can be a bit confusing. Files on
disk have an apparent size, which indicates how much bytes are in the file from
the users point of view; this is the size reported by tools like `ls -l`. The
apparent size can be any number, from 0 bytes up to several TB.  The actual
number of bytes which are used on the filesystem to store the file can differ
from this apparent size for a number of reasons: disks store data in blocks,
which cause files to always take up a multiple of the block size, files can
have holes ('sparse' files), and other technical reasons. This number is always
a multiple of 512, which means that the actual size used for a file is almost
always a bit more than its apparent size.

Duc has two modes for counting file sizes:

- `apparent size`: this is the size as reported by `ls`. This number indicates
  the file length, which is usually smaller than the actual disk usage. 

- `actual size`: this is the size as reported by `du` and `df`. The actual file
  size tells you how much disk is actually used by a file, and is always a
  multiple of 512 bytes. 

The default mode used by duc is to use the 'actual size'. Most duc

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

* What does the error 'Database version mismatch mean?'
 
  The layout of the index database sometimes changes when new features are
  implemented. When you get this error you have probably upgraded to a newer
  version. Just remove the old database file and rebuild the index.

* Duc crashes with a segmentation fault, is it that buggy?

  By default Duc uses the Tokyocabinet database backend. Tokyocabinet is pretty
  fast, stores the database in a single file and has nice compression support
  to keep the database small. Unfortunately, it is not always robust and
  sometimes chokes on corrupt database files. Try to remove the database
  and rebuild the index. If the error persists contact the authors.

* Some of the Duc subcommands like `duc gui` are not available on my system?

  Depending on the configuration that was chosen when building Duc, some
  options might or might not be available in the `duc` utility. For example, on
  Debian or Ubuntu Duc comes in two flavours: there is a full featured package
  called `duc`, or a package without dependencies on X-windows called
  `duc-nox`, for which the latter lacks the `duc gui` command.

* `duc index` is hogging my system and using a lot of CPU and I/O!

  Traversing a file system is hard work - which is the exact reason why Duc
  exists in the first place. You can use the default tools to make Duc behave
  nice towards other processes on your machine, use something like:

  `nice 19 ionice -c 3 duc index [options]`

  This makes `duc index` run with the lowest CPU and I/O scheduler priorities,
  which is nicer to all the other processes on your machine.


## FILES

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

Duc mainains an index of scanned directories, which defaults to ~/.duc.db. All tools
take the -d/--database option to override the database path.

# config handling
def read_config_database(subcmd):
    # returns database path from config if any, else None
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    # parse option
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    # normalize opt: remove leading dashes
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            # only take if section matches global or subcmd
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                        elif section in (None,"global",subcmd):
                            # no val? ignore
                            pass
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        # expand ~
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    # default per original: ~/.cache/duc/duc.db
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    # returns connection or None and error type
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        # try simple query
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        msg=str(e).lower()
        if "malformed" in msg or "not a database" in msg or "file is not a database" in msg or "no such table" in msg:
            # check file header is SQLite?
            try:
                with open(path,'rb') as f:
                    header=f.read(16)
                    if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                        return None, "corrupt"
            except:
                pass
            # need to distinguish corrupt vs not_found? For our case, any DatabaseError treat as corrupt
            return None, "corrupt"
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    # command determines whether second line printed
    # For ls, gui, ui : only first line
    # For others: two lines
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        pass
    else:
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_readable(size):
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def human_bucket(size):
    # for histogram bucket header
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        if size % 1024 == 0:
            return f"{size//1024:.1f}K".replace(".0K",".0K")  # but original shows 1.0K not 1K
        else:
            return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    # floor log2
    return sz.bit_length()-1

def error_unrecognized(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: unrecognized option '{opt}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def error_invalid(opt_char):
    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: invalid option -- '{opt_char}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def need_value(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: option '{opt}' requires an argument")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_common_global(args):
    # returns dict of global opts and remaining args after consuming globals?
    # This is for handling --debug etc after subcommand
    globals_opts = {"debug":False,"verbose":False,"quiet":False}
    # we will just detect presence
    for a in args:
        if a=="--debug":
            globals_opts["debug"]=True
        elif a in ("--verbose","-v"):
            globals_opts["verbose"]=True
        elif a in ("--quiet","-q"):
            globals_opts["quiet"]=True
    return globals_opts

# config handling
def read_config_database(subcmd):
    # returns database path from config if any, else None
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    # parse option
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    # normalize opt: remove leading dashes
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            # only take if section matches global or subcmd
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                        elif section in (None,"global",subcmd):
                            # no val? ignore
                            pass
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        # expand ~
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    # default per original: ~/.cache/duc/duc.db
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    # returns connection or None and error type
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        # try simple query
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        msg=str(e).lower()
        if "malformed" in msg or "not a database" in msg or "file is not a database" in msg or "no such table" in msg:
            # check file header is SQLite?
            try:
                with open(path,'rb') as f:
                    header=f.read(16)
                    if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                        return None, "corrupt"
            except:
                pass
            # need to distinguish corrupt vs not_found? For our case, any DatabaseError treat as corrupt
            return None, "corrupt"
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    # command determines whether second line printed
    # For ls, gui, ui : only first line
    # For others: two lines
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        pass
    else:
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_readable(size):
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def human_bucket(size):
    # for histogram bucket header
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        if size % 1024 == 0:
            return f"{size//1024:.1f}K".replace(".0K",".0K")  # but original shows 1.0K not 1K
        else:
            return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    # floor log2
    return sz.bit_length()-1

    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: option '{opt}' requires an argument")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_common_global(args):
    # returns dict of global opts and remaining args after consuming globals?
    # This is for handling --debug etc after subcommand
    globals_opts = {"debug":False,"verbose":False,"quiet":False}
    # we will just detect presence
    for a in args:
        if a=="--debug":
            globals_opts["debug"]=True
        elif a in ("--verbose","-v"):
            globals_opts["verbose"]=True
        elif a in ("--quiet","-q"):
            globals_opts["quiet"]=True
    return globals_opts

def eprint(s):
    print(s, file=sys.stderr)

def prog():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else "duc"

def read_config_database(subcmd):
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        msg=str(e).lower()
        # check header
        try:
            with open(path,'rb') as f:
                header=f.read(16)
                if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                    return None, "corrupt"
        except:
            pass
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        pass
    else:
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_size(size):
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    return sz.bit_length()-1

def parse_global_flags(args):
    flags={"debug":False,"verbose":False,"quiet":False}
    for a in args:
        if a=="--debug":
            flags["debug"]=True
        elif a in ("--verbose","-v"):
            flags["verbose"]=True
        elif a in ("--quiet","-q"):
            flags["quiet"]=True
    return flags

def error_unrecognized(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: unrecognized option '{opt}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def error_invalid(ch):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: invalid option -- '{ch}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def need_value(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: option '{opt}' requires an argument")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def eprint(s):
    print(s, file=sys.stderr)

def prog():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else "duc"

def read_config_database(subcmd):
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        msg=str(e).lower()
        # check header
        try:
            with open(path,'rb') as f:
                header=f.read(16)
                if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                    return None, "corrupt"
        except:
            pass
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        pass
    else:
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_size(size):
    if size < 1024:
        return str(size)
    elif size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f}K"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    return sz.bit_length()-1

def parse_global_flags(args):
    flags={"debug":False,"verbose":False,"quiet":False}
    for a in args:
        if a=="--debug":
            flags["debug"]=True
        elif a in ("--verbose","-v"):
            flags["verbose"]=True
        elif a in ("--quiet","-q"):
            flags["quiet"]=True
    return flags

def error_unrecognized(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: unrecognized option '{opt}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def error_invalid(ch):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: invalid option -- '{ch}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def need_value(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: option '{opt}' requires an argument")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def prog():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else "duc"

def eprint(s):
    print(s, file=sys.stderr)

def read_config_database(subcmd):
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        try:
            with open(path,'rb') as f:
                header=f.read(16)
                if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                    return None, "corrupt"
        except:
            pass
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command not in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_size(sz):
    if sz < 1024:
        return str(sz)
    elif sz < 1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/1024:.1f}K"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    return sz.bit_length()-1

def error_unrecognized(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: unrecognized option '{opt}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def error_invalid(ch):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: invalid option -- '{ch}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def prog():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else "duc"

def eprint(s):
    print(s, file=sys.stderr)

def read_config_database(subcmd):
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db = None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section = None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts:
                        continue
                    opt=parts[0]
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    opt=opt.lstrip("-")
                    if opt=="database":
                        if val:
                            if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                                db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        except:
            continue
    return db

def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env = os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg = read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")

def open_db(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur = con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs table")
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:
        try:
            with open(path,'rb') as f:
                header=f.read(16)
                if not header.startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                    return None, "corrupt"
        except:
            pass
        return None, "corrupt"
    except Exception:
        return None, "corrupt"

def db_error_message(path, err_type):
    if err_type=="not_found":
        return "Database not found"
    elif err_type=="corrupt":
        return "Database corrupt and not usable"
    return "Database error"

def print_db_error(path, err_type, command):
    first = f"Error opening: {path} - {db_error_message(path, err_type)}"
    eprint(first)
    if command not in ("ls","gui","ui"):
        eprint(db_error_message(path, err_type))

def human_size(sz):
    if sz < 1024:
        return str(sz)
    elif sz < 1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/1024:.1f}K"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024):.1f}M"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024):.1f}G"
    elif sz < 1024*1024*1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}T"
    else:
        return f"{sz/(1024*1024*1024*1024*1024):.1f}P"

def bucket_for_size(sz):
    if sz <= 0:
        return 0
    return sz.bit_length()-1

def error_unrecognized(opt):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: unrecognized option '{opt}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

def error_invalid(ch):
    eprint(f"{prog()}: invalid option -- '{ch}'")
    eprint("Try 'duc --help' for more information.")
    sys.exit(1)

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the section in square brackets and
continues until the next section begins. Sections contain parameters, one per
line, which consist of a single option name for boolean flags, or an option name
and a value for options which take a value. See the EXAMPLES section for an
example of the configuration file format.


## CREATING THE INDEX

Duc needs an index file of the file system before it is able to show any
information.  To create the index, run the `duc index` command. For example, to
create an index of your home directory run `duc index ~`

    $ duc index /usr
    Skipping lost+found: Permission denied
    Indexed 333823 files and 48200 directories, (35.0GB total) in 1 seconds

The default location of the database is `$HOME/.duc.db`. To use a different
database location, use the DUC_DATABASE environment variable or specify the
database location with the --database argument.

You can run `duc index` at any time later to rebuild the index.

By default Duc indexes all directories it encounters during file system
traversal, including special file systems like /proc and /sys, and
network file systems like NFS or Samba mounts. There are a few options to
select what parts of your filesystem you want to include or exclude from the
scan, check the documentation below for the options --one-file-system, 
--exclude, --fs-exclude and --fs-include for more details.


## QUERYING THE INDEX

Duc has various subcommands for querying or exploring the index: (Note that
depending on your configuration, some of these commands might not be available)

* `duc info` shows a list of available directory trees in the database, and the time
  and date of the last scan.

* `duc ls` lists all files and directories under the given path on the console.

* `duc ui` runs a ncurses based console user interface for exploring the file
  system usage.

* `duc gui` starts a graphical (X11) interface representing the file system in
  a sunburst graph. Click on a directory to redraw the graph from the
  perspective of the selected directory. Click in the center of the graph to go
  up one directory in the tree.


## OPTIONS

This section list all available subcommands and describes their usage and options.

def read_config_database(subcmd):
    files = ["/etc/ducrc", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/duc/ducrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.ducrc"), "./.ducrc"]
    db=None
    for f in files:
        if not os.path.exists(f):
            continue
        try:
            with open(f) as fp:
                section=None
                for line in fp:
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
                        continue
                    if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                        section=line[1:-1].strip()
                        continue
                    parts=line.split(None,1)
                    if not parts: continue
                    opt=parts[0].lstrip("-")
                    val=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else None
                    if opt=="database" and val:
                        if section is None or section=="global" or section==subcmd:
                            db=val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        except: continue
    return db
def get_db_path(subcmd, cli_db):
    if cli_db:
        return cli_db
    env=os.environ.get("DUC_DATABASE")
    if env:
        return env
    cfg=read_config_database(subcmd)
    if cfg:
        return os.path.expanduser(cfg)
    return os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/duc/duc.db")
def open_db(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "not_found"
    try:
        con=sqlite3.connect(path)
        cur=con.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='blobs'")
        if cur.fetchone()[0]==0:
            raise sqlite3.DatabaseError("no blobs")
        cur.execute("SELECT key FROM blobs LIMIT 1")
        cur.fetchall()
        return con, None
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError:
        try:
            with open(path,'rb') as f:
                if not f.read(16).startswith(b"SQLite format 3"):
                    return None, "corrupt"
        except: pass
        return None, "corrupt"
    except: return None, "corrupt"

    if sz<1024:

    elif sz<1024*1024:

    elif sz<1024*1024*1024:

def handle_global_help_version():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if "--version" in argv:
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION)
        sys.exit(0)
    help_indices = [i for i, tok in enumerate(argv) if tok in ("--help","-h")]
    if not help_indices:
        return
    first_help = help_indices[0]
    if argv and argv[0] in ("--debug","--verbose","-v","--quiet","-q"):
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_HELP)
        sys.exit(0)
    if len(help_indices) >= 2:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_HELP)
        sys.exit(0)
    has_all = any(tok in ("--all","-a") for tok in argv)
    target_after = None
    for tok in argv[first_help+1:]:
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            continue
        if tok in KNOWN:
            target_after = tok
            break
        if not tok.startswith("-"):
            break
    if target_after is not None:
        mapping = {"ls":HELP_LS,"index":HELP_INDEX,"info":HELP_INFO,"histogram":HELP_HISTOGRAM,"topn":HELP_TOPN,"xml":HELP_XML,"json":HELP_JSON,"graph":HELP_GRAPH,"cgi":HELP_CGI,"gui":HELP_GUI,"ui":HELP_UI,"help":HELP_HELP}
        if target_after in mapping:
            sys.stdout.write(mapping[target_after])
            sys.exit(0)
    target_before = None
    for tok in reversed(argv[:first_help]):
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            continue
        if tok in KNOWN:
            target_before = tok
            break
        if not tok.startswith("-"):
            break
    if target_before is not None:
        mapping = {"ls":HELP_LS,"index":HELP_INDEX,"info":HELP_INFO,"histogram":HELP_HISTOGRAM,"topn":HELP_TOPN,"xml":HELP_XML,"json":HELP_JSON,"graph":HELP_GRAPH,"cgi":HELP_CGI,"gui":HELP_GUI,"ui":HELP_UI,"help":HELP_HELP}
        if target_before in mapping:
            sys.stdout.write(mapping[target_before])
            sys.exit(0)
    if has_all:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_ALL)
        sys.exit(0)
    sys.stdout.write(MAIN_HELP)
